title: Bending Aluminum Tube: How to Bend 6061 Without Cracking
excerpt: Bending aluminum tube without cracks: 6061 tempers (O, T4, T6), safe bend radius, roller pressure dies, annealing trade-offs and a step-by-step method.

notes: Direct page fetches were blocked, so all Rogue Fab, The Fabricator and ESAB facts came from WebSearch result summaries of those pages; please spot-check: (1) Rogue Fab aluminum page: 3.5D-4D target, 3D 'on the edge' with extra cracking risk for 6061-T6, 1.25 OD examples (4.5 CLR = 3.6D, 6.0 CLR = 4.8D, less thinning/cracking), annealing as the usual fix, 6063 more forgiving (lower strength, higher elongation), steel dies mark aluminum esp. pre-anodized, roller dies reduce force; (2) Rogue Fab FAQ: friction pressure die 'cannot run aluminum, it galls', roller die works on all materials; Bender Tech page mentions UHMW pressure dies; TWR page warns of a ridge/dent on .125 6061; (3) The Fabricator Aluminum Workshop column: 6061-T4/6063-T4 about 2.5x tube diameter, T6 at least 4x, alloy ranking 1100-O...6061-T6; extrusion article: T4 max for tight radii; Bending Aluminum 101: re-temper to T6 needs solution treat + quench + artificial age, soot torch-anneal method, aluminum shows no colour change; (4) ESAB 'Using heat with aluminum alloys': example ~45,000 psi before welding vs ~27,000 psi as-welded, common fillers don't respond to PWHT unless heavily diluted. Conflict flagged in text: Rogue Fab allows 3.5D for 6061-T6, The Fabricator column says 4x minimum for T6. Temper definitions (T4 naturally aged, T6 artificially aged) are standard designations, seen in a supplier datasheet summary. Left out: annealing and re-heat-treat temperatures/times (sheet-focused, search-summary only), sheet springback figures, any aluminum tube springback number (none published), 3003/5052 bending guidance (not found). Eastwood aluminum rating is from the 21115Q manual via the kit fact-check notes. Worked D-of-bend values in the radius table are simple arithmetic.
